posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
Easy mint.

I just beat him down, ignoring everything else. He had 2x Wagelings at the start, so there was the possibility he’d get out a 3rd wageling and outnumber the heroes, but with Unity on the team I figured I’d generally have at least one bot in play. He did play Losing To The Odds on turn 2, and I did the “punch Unity with Guise” thing to even out everyone’s HP, but a Skunk Ape came out and upset the math. I realized that there were too many damaging Cryptids in the environment deck to make HP-stacking for Losing To The Odds to be a decent bet, so I just concentrated on damage.

It helped a lot that Guise got the Guise the Barbarian / Blatant Reference combo early. With Wager Master as a nemesis, that meant 4 points of damage a turn, for a total of 16 including the 4 from Tough Choices. Scholar had a couple of Grace Under Fires, which were good for 4-5 damage each between the Wagelings and environment targets. Unity finished him off with Turret Bot and Platform Bot.

He did get a couple of What Do You Really Know?’s in play, which between them knocked Guise and Unity down to 4-5 HP each, which could have been bad if I took much longer to knock him out.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
To my AAR I have to add:

I don’t much like randomized Wager Master challenges. Given how ridiculously random Wager Master games are, with turn-2 wins from “Losing to the Odds” being fairly common vs. games which are nigh impossible because of Who Are You Fighting, a randomized start means that comparing war stories  after the challenge is pointless. Some people are going to have trivial games which teach nothing, and some are going to Kobayashi Maru games which no amount of clever play can salvage. With most villain match-ups we can talk strategy and clever tricks, but with Wager Master strategy doesn’t rise much above plays to take advantage of Losing To The Odds.

posts.name: QuirkyDM
posts.cooked:
Took me 3 tries. I almost had him on the first try, getting him to low health and then pulling Guise's +2 to damage, shoot stuff at the end of each turn combo. Then I flipped Wager Master to get rid of his "lose if Wager Master is at 0 health" condition. Unfortunately, Guise pretty much buried himself by damaging himself for 3 on each of the conditions that flipped. I lost shortly thereafter.

Game 2 was nothing to write home about. Everyone took a lot of damage and that was that.

Game 3, Stealth Bot and Scholar tanked a lot. With Stealth Bot, it's easy to redirect damage as needed to get everyone at even hit points at the right time, which is what happened, and I finally won.

I enjoy Wager Master, but it is completely unpredictable what's going to happen.

I admit to being annoyed enough to cheat a bit during my second play through  - Losing to the Odds came out pretty quickly but flipped at the start of the turn so I couldn't win with it (since it needs to be at the end of the turn to win). The Scholar used Offensive Transmutation to make sure Wager Master wouldn't do anything to mess up my HP. Everyone was at even numbers until an Amphibious Chupacabra showed up and did 3 points of damage to Unity. So I had no problem with rewinding to her turn and having her lightning damage herself for one point of damage to make sure she'd be back at even during Wager Master's turn.

If he can cheat and take away my Mint, then I'm going to make sure I take advantage of the ability to rewind.
